mainEntity.name: Do you charge if my data cannot be recovered?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Data Doctor Hub offers a free diagnosis and a no-recovery, no-charge policy. A quote is confirmed before recovery work begins, and you pay only if the data you approve is recovered.

mainEntity.name: How long does data recovery take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Diagnosis is provided within 48 hours. Typical options are standard recovery in 5–7 days, priority in 2–3 days, and emergency service in 24 hours. Timing depends on the device and damage.

mainEntity.name: Can you recover data from a MacBook that won't turn on?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. On T2 and Apple silicon (M1–M4) Macs the SSD is soldered to the logic board and hardware-encrypted, so the storage can't simply be removed and read elsewhere. We repair the original logic board at component level so the Mac can start, then copy your data off. You'll need your Mac login or FileVault password.

mainEntity.name: My MacBook had a liquid spill. What should I do?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switch it off, unplug the charger, and don't try to power it on again. Each attempt can spread corrosion or short components. Contact us on WhatsApp or call +91 98458 63602 — the sooner the board is cleaned, the better the chance of recovery.

mainEntity.name: Which devices can Data Doctor Hub recover data from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hard drives, SSDs and NVMe drives, MacBooks, iMacs and other Macs, RAID and server storage, Windows laptops and desktops, USB drives, SD cards, mobile phones and tablets.

mainEntity.name: Is my data kept confidential during recovery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Data Doctor Hub describes its process as confidential and NDA-backed. Customer data stays within its secure facility and is not transferred unencrypted.

mainEntity.name: Can I contact you on WhatsApp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Message +91 98458 63602 on WhatsApp to describe the problem, send photos of the device, or ask for an update on your case.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer device pickup?

acceptedAnswer.text: Data Doctor Hub advertises free doorstep pickup across its service locations. Contact the recovery team to confirm pickup availability for your area.

mainEntity.name: Where are Data Doctor Hub's offices in Bengaluru?

acceptedAnswer.text: Data Doctor Hub has two locations in Bengaluru 560002: #31, Ground Floor, Luciya City Center, OTC Road, Bengaluru-560002; and Building no 6, Shop no #3, Ground Floor, Electronic Plaza, 3rd Cross, P.R. Lane, SP Road, Bengaluru 560002. Call +91 98458 63602 before visiting for consultation and drop-off arrangements.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer on-site data recovery for companies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. For registered businesses and organisations, Data Doctor Hub engineers can recover data at your office, server room or data centre, so sensitive data never leaves your premises. It covers RAID arrays, NAS and SAN storage, VMware and Hyper-V servers, database servers and workstations. An NDA is signed before the visit, and drives with physical damage are taken to the cleanroom lab under a chain-of-custody record. On-site service isn't available for individual customers. Request an on-site visit.

mainEntity.name: Can you recover deleted or overwritten CCTV footage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in many cases. Data Doctor Hub recovers deleted, formatted and partly overwritten footage from DVRs, NVRs, DVR hard drives and camera SD cards, including Hikvision, Dahua and CP Plus, and delivers it as playable video with timestamps. Stop the recording as soon as you need old footage. CCTV footage recovery.

mainEntity.name: Can you restore files after a ransomware attack?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes, without paying the ransom. Data Doctor Hub restores files from deleted originals, shadow copies, partly encrypted files, damaged backups and known free decryptors, for PCs, servers, NAS and Tally or SQL databases. Disconnect infected systems from the network and don't wipe anything. Ransomware file restoration.

mainEntity.name: How much does data recovery cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost depends on the device, its capacity and the type of damage, so Data Doctor Hub gives an exact quote after a free diagnosis. You confirm the quote before work starts, and if the data can't be recovered there is no charge.

mainEntity.name: Can data be recovered from a phone that won't turn on?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually, yes. When a phone is dead, the photos and chats are normally still on its memory chip. Because modern phones are encrypted with keys tied to their own processor, Data Doctor Hub repairs the original board at component level so the phone can start, then copies the data off with the owner's passcode.

mainEntity.name: Can you recover data from a water-damaged phone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, if it is brought in quickly. Switch the phone off and don't charge it; skip the bag of rice, which doesn't stop corrosion. Data Doctor Hub cleans the corrosion from the board, replaces damaged parts and recovers the data.

mainEntity.name: My phone's screen is broken. Can I still get my photos?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in most cases. If the phone still works underneath, a working screen is connected temporarily so the phone can be unlocked with your passcode and everything copied off. If the screen damage also affected the board, it is repaired first.

mainEntity.name: Can deleted WhatsApp chats be recovered?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes. The best source is usually a WhatsApp backup in Google Drive (Android) or iCloud (iPhone), which can be restored to a phone. Data Doctor Hub checks every available backup and the phone itself, and tells you what can be restored before you pay.

mainEntity.name: Can data be recovered after a factory reset?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not from a modern phone itself. A factory reset on current iPhones and Android phones destroys the encryption keys, so the old data can no longer be read. Photos and chats may still be recoverable from iCloud, Google Photos, Google Drive, WhatsApp or computer backups, which Data Doctor Hub can help you check.

mainEntity.name: I forgot my phone's passcode. Can you unlock it?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Data Doctor Hub does not crack or bypass phone passcodes. Without the passcode, data on a modern encrypted phone cannot be read by any honest lab. What can often be recovered instead is any data backed up to your Apple or Google account.

mainEntity.name: Which phone brands do you recover data from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Data Doctor Hub recovers data from Apple iPhones and iPads, and from Android phones and tablets by Samsung, OnePlus, Xiaomi, Redmi, POCO, Vivo, iQOO, OPPO, Realme, Google Pixel, Motorola, Nokia, Nothing and others, plus their microSD memory cards.

mainEntity.name: How long does phone data recovery take, and what does it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Diagnosis is free and usually done within 48 hours. Most recoveries take 2–5 days; liquid damage and complex board repairs can take longer. The price depends on the fault and is confirmed before any work starts. If the data can't be recovered, there is no charge.

mainEntity.name: Are my photos and chats kept private?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Data Doctor Hub handles phone data confidentially, looks at files only as far as needed to confirm the recovery with you, and securely deletes its working copies after handover.

mainEntity.name: Can deleted CCTV footage be recovered?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually, yes. When footage is deleted from a DVR or NVR, the video data normally stays on the hard drive until new recordings overwrite it. Data Doctor Hub reads the drive directly, rebuilds the recorder's index and recovers the clips with their camera number and timestamps. The sooner recording is stopped, the better the chances.

mainEntity.name: Can overwritten CCTV footage be recovered?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only partly. When a DVR records over the same space, the old video there is permanently replaced. However, loop recording rarely overwrites everything evenly, so fragments of the older footage often survive between new recordings. After a free diagnosis, Data Doctor Hub tells you exactly which cameras and time ranges are recoverable.

mainEntity.name: My DVR was formatted or reset. Is the footage lost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. A quick format or factory reset usually clears the DVR's index, not the video itself. If the recorder was switched off soon afterwards, most of the footage can often be recovered. Don't let it keep recording, and don't format it again.

mainEntity.name: Which DVR and NVR brands do you support?

acceptedAnswer.text: Data Doctor Hub recovers footage from Hikvision, Dahua, CP Plus, Uniview, Honeywell, Godrej, Zicom, Prama, Bosch, Axis, Panasonic and most other DVRs and NVRs, as well as SD cards from Wi-Fi cameras and dashcams.

mainEntity.name: My DVR won't switch on after a power surge. What now?

acceptedAnswer.text: The footage is stored on the DVR's hard drive, which often survives when the recorder's power board fails. Bring the DVR or just its hard drive to the lab; the drive is read directly without needing the recorder to work. Don't keep trying to power it on.

mainEntity.name: Can the recovered footage be used for police or insurance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Data Doctor Hub delivers recovered clips with MD5 and SHA-256 hash values and, on request, a written recovery report and chain-of-custody record. Whether evidence is accepted is decided by the police, insurer or court, but this documentation shows how the footage was recovered and that it hasn't been altered.

mainEntity.name: How long does CCTV footage recovery take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Diagnosis is usually completed within 48 hours, and urgent cases can be prioritised. Simple deleted-footage cases are often finished in 2–3 days; physically failed drives or multi-drive NVRs can take longer. You'll get a time estimate with the quote.

mainEntity.name: How much does CCTV data recovery cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The diagnosis is free. The price depends on the recorder, drive size and the damage, so Data Doctor Hub confirms an exact quote before starting. If the footage can't be recovered, there's no charge.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to bring the whole DVR?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bringing the DVR with its power adapter is best, because it helps confirm the recorder's settings. If that's difficult, the hard drive alone is enough in most cases. Data Doctor Hub's labs are near SP Road, Bengaluru, and pickup can be arranged.

mainEntity.name: Can files encrypted by ransomware be recovered without paying?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. Many ransomware strains delete the original files after writing encrypted copies, encrypt only part of each file, or leave shadow copies and backups behind. Data Doctor Hub recovers deleted originals, rebuilds partly encrypted files, restores snapshots and backups, and applies known free decryptors where they exist. A free assessment shows what is recoverable before any payment.

mainEntity.name: Do you pay the ransom or negotiate with the attackers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Data Doctor Hub never pays ransoms, contacts attackers or negotiates on a customer's behalf. Recovery is done only with technical methods, working on forensic copies of the affected drives.

mainEntity.name: Which ransomware variants can you recover from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Data Doctor Hub works with files hit by LockBit, Phobos, Makop, STOP/Djvu, Dharma (CrySIS), Mallox, Akira, BlackCat (ALPHV), Medusa, Babuk, Conti, QNAP DeadBolt and Qlocker, and others. What can be restored depends on how the specific attack behaved, not just the variant's name.

mainEntity.name: Is there a free decryptor for my ransomware?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes. Security researchers publish free decryptors for some variants, many listed on the No More Ransom project. Data Doctor Hub identifies the exact variant from the ransom note and an encrypted sample, and tests any available decryptor safely on copies of your files.

mainEntity.name: What should I do immediately after a ransomware attack?

acceptedAnswer.text: Disconnect infected systems from the network, or power them off if you can't isolate them. Don't reinstall Windows, format drives, run clean-up tools or rename encrypted files. Keep the ransom note, don't contact the attackers, and call a recovery specialist. Report the crime on the 1930 helpline or at cybercrime.gov.in.

mainEntity.name: Can encrypted Tally, SQL Server or other database files be restored?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many cases. Large database and Tally files are often only partly encrypted, so their data can be rebuilt from the unencrypted parts and checked for consistency. Deleted originals and older copies on the same drive are also searched.

mainEntity.name: Our NAS (QNAP or Synology) was hit. Can the data be recovered?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. NAS attacks such as DeadBolt or Qlocker frequently leave snapshots, unencrypted remnants or recoverable originals on the disks. The drives are removed and imaged in the lab, and the RAID volume is rebuilt from the images.

mainEntity.name: How long does ransomware recovery take, and what does it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Data Doctor Hub aims to complete the free assessment within 24–48 hours, and business-critical cases are prioritised. The quote depends on the number of systems, the data volume and the method needed, and it is confirmed before work starts. If nothing can be recovered, there is no charge.

mainEntity.name: Should I report a ransomware attack?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. In India, report it on the National Cyber Crime Helpline 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in. Organisations may also need to report cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing them. Data Doctor Hub can provide an incident report to support these reports and insurance claims.
